attempts.strategy: Split on indicator activity and on whether the stopping time is top; prove inactive branch by constant-zero continuity, top branch by congruence with the original path, and finite branch by composing original continuity with s ↦ min s a.
attempts.code_tried: by_cases hω : (⊥ : κ) < τ ω; by_cases htop : τ ω = ⊤; obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := WithTop.ne_top_iff_exists.mp htop; refine (hcont.comp' hg_cont hg_maps).congr ?_; rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hmem, ← ha, ← WithTop.coe_min, WithTop.untopA_coe]
attempts.goal_before: ContinuousOn ((stoppedProcess (fun i ↦ {ω | (⊥ : κ) < τ ω}.indicator (N i)) τ) · ω) (Set.Icc (⊥ : κ) t) from hcont : ContinuousOn (N · ω) (Set.Icc (⊥ : κ) t)
attempts.insight: For fixed ω, the indicator is constant in time. If τ ω is finite, stopping is composition with the continuous coordinate map s ↦ min s a; if τ ω is top or inactive, the path is respectively the original path or zero.

next_steps: Use this helper to replace explicit stopped-piece continuity hypotheses by original-process continuity in the next localizing-sequence wrapper; keep mesh and variation bounds explicit.
